questions.q: The intensity of light from a continuously emitting laser source operating at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>638</mn><mi>nm</mi></math> wavelength is modulated at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi>GHz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The modulation is done by momentarily cutting the intensity off with a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi>GHz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> What is the farthest distance apart two detectors can be placed in the line of the laser light, so that they can see the portions of the same pulse simultaneously? (Consider the speed of light in air <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open=""><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>:</mo></math>
questions.solution:
Time period between two flashes =1f
Distance travelled by laser in this interval
=cf=3×108109=0.3 m=30 cm

So this is the maximum distance between two detectors, so that they can see the same pulse simultaneously.

When the circuit is placed in a uniform electric field, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> perpendicular to the plane (inward) of the circuit and the rod is pulled to the right with a constant speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the "magnetic EMF" in the current and the direction of the corresponding current, arising because of changing electric flux will be (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>l</mi></math> is the length of the rod and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> is speed of light ).
questions.solution:

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves emanating from a point $\mathrm{A}$ (in air) are incident on a rectangular block of material $\mathrm{M}$ and emerge from the other side as shown. The angles $\mathrm{I}$ and $\mathrm{r}$ are angles of incidence and refraction when the wave travels from air to the medium. Such paths for the rays are possible
options: if the material has a refractive index very nearly equal to zero
only with gamma rays with a wavelength smaller than atomic nuclei of the material
if the material has a refractive index less than zero
only if the wave travels in $M$ with a speed faster than the speed of light in vacuum.
questions.solution: It is possible for negative $\mu$ only and materials are known as meta materials.
